analysis.title: GS Coppersmith - US EQUITIES the flight to quality 12 Oct 2026
key_insights: SPX is within 1% of all-time highs, but the median S&P stock is 16% below its own high. GS breadth is at its weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble.
The GS Quality factor has rallied more than 16% over 8 weeks, the largest move since the COVID shock in 2020, which signals more risk aversion under the surface than the index shows.
Coppersmith does not read market narrowness as a warning sign and favors SPX higher over the next 1-3 months.

Bloomberg found 13 episodes since 1995 where the 10 largest S&P stocks beat equal weight by more than 8% over three months. Median subsequent SPX returns were +10.1% over 6 months and +19.6% over 12 months, against historical medians of +6.9% and +15%. The current gap is 855bps.
The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator is at -1.3, a level where forward returns look more attractive. Positioning is light for a market near its highs.

Global fundamental L/S net leverage is in the 6th percentile over the past year (2nd percentile for the US). Overall HF net leverage is in the 10th percentile. Gross exposures remain relatively elevated.
Fundamental L/S funds lost 70bps between October 2-8 on negative alpha from both longs and shorts. US single stocks were net sold for a third straight week, with short sales outpacing long buys.

Tech flipped from the most net bought sector in four of the prior five weeks to by far the most net sold last week, through long sales and incremental shorting. Tech's L/S ratio is 1.8 (17th percentile over five years) while gross allocation is in the 97th percentile.

Industrials saw their fastest buying since January (+1.8 SD), almost entirely new longs after five weeks of selling. Their L/S ratio is in the 22nd percentile over five years. Financials also saw buying and Software showed relative strength.

Staples has been net sold in seven of the past eight weeks, entirely through shorting, with its L/S ratio in the 3rd percentile over five years. Biotech had its largest cumulative eight-week de-grossing in more than five years.
After 10-year yields moved above 5%, the GS Rates team sees asymmetry skewed toward lower yields, and rates vol has started to reverse. Stability in Treasuries would be enough to help equities.

GS Commodities expects Brent to moderate toward $90 by December and average $80 in 2027, but sees risks skewed meaningfully higher, especially near term. More than $20/bbl of risk premium is still embedded in prices.
NVDA downside implied volatility is at levels not seen since before Covid, which Coppersmith frames as a hedging opportunity against an AI-trade unwind or crowding in quality.
Overall view: earnings are supportive, positioning is light, and extreme concentration alone is not a reason to turn bearish. Oil and rates are the main risks.

tension_points.bull_case: Extreme concentration has historically been bullish. After 13 episodes since 1995, median SPX returns were +10.1% over 6 months and +19.6% over 12 months. Positioning is light and earnings are supportive.
tension_points.bear_case: The median S&P stock is 16% below its high, breadth is the weakest since the Dot-Com Bubble, and the Quality factor rallied more than 16% in 8 weeks, which signals risk aversion beneath the index.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Another meaningful move higher in both oil and rates.
